Responsible Release of AI-Generated Mathematics

At present, some frontier AI labs are testing advanced mathematical problems on proprietary models that remain inaccessible to the broader scientific community. Our recommendations are formulated with this practical context in mind. However, ideally, they would not do so. We want to state clearly from the start: we do not endorse this practice, and we ask them to stop testing advanced mathematical problems on proprietary models.

The mathematical community has long-standing norms concerning the dissemination and peer review of results. These norms have been essential for the reliability, trustworthiness, and effectiveness of mathematical work. One of the most important scholarly norms in mathematics is that the authors of a paper should understand the mathematical argument of that paper, have verified its correctness themselves, and take full responsibility for the content. Moreover, in the mathematical community, authors of works that significantly advance the field regularly give seminars at other institutions and talks at conferences, explaining their new developments and answering questions from colleagues. This all works towards developing the deepest possible human understanding of mathematics, which is one of the crowning glories of millennia of human development.

However, it is now the case that AI can output mathematical arguments in situations without the human who prompted it being able to understand the arguments, verify them, or take responsibility for them. We believe that human understanding of mathematics remains of paramount importance. How, in this new era, can we work towards a new paradigm that includes human understanding of mathematics as part of responsible scholarly output?

We asked the mathematical community for feedback about what it would mean for AI labs to responsibly release mathematical results 1 and received over 600 replies. Informed by these responses, we arrived at a set of recommendations, supported by a clear plurality of respondents, aimed at any AI lab whose models are likely to have a significant impact on mathematics. The overarching principles underlying these recommendations are the following.

We present our recommendations themselves in Section 2, and in Section 3 we make some comments about access to powerful models.

2. Responsible release of results generated by AI labs

We recommend two possible courses of action, depending on the level of human understanding that accompanies a result.

2.A. Papers that a human understands

Papers for which there is a mathematician responsible who fully understands the content should follow the academic mathematical community’s traditional norms: the mathematician(s) concerned should post a preprint, submit a paper for peer review at a journal, and give talks to explain the work to other mathematicians.

2.B. Papers that are not yet understood by anybody

The recommendations below are for labs that have AI mathematical output that is not understood by the people who prompted the AI systems. They are split into two parts. The first part is a set of proposed technical norms for the release of AI-generated mathematics. The second part is a recommendation that AI labs provide support for the additional mathematical activities that are needed for humans to be able to understand and assimilate their AI-generated mathematical output and identify possible applications of it.

1. With the help of LLMs, it is easy to make substantial improvements to the initial written version of an AI-generated result. The following actions should be carried out by the AI labs rather than left to mathematicians afterwards.

(a) The literature should be scoured for any ideas that are related to the ideas in the proofs of the results released. Even if the AI lab’s model discovered those ideas independently, it should follow standard mathematical practice and cite the papers in which the ideas were first introduced.

(b) The model, or some other model, should be prompted to produce a version of each proof that is written up in a style that follows the conventions of a traditional mathematical paper. They should contain friendly introductions and precise theorem statements and proofs. They should not be full of wordy reasoning and non-standard terminology that renders them virtually incomprehensible.

The current abilities of LLMs may not be able to reproduce the level of attribution or quality of exposition that we expect of mathematicians, and thus more important work from mathematicians after release may be needed to reach this standard. If so, this should be supported as described in Step II. However, inability to reach a high standard does not absolve AI labs of the responsibility to do the best they can with their models on the two points above.

2. When results are announced, they should be deposited in a timely manner in appropriate scholarly repositories. These should not be controlled by any AI lab and should guarantee certain standards, including that submissions have a persistent citable identifier and that subsequent modifications are appropriately recorded. For AI-generated results, it would be particularly useful if the repository allows for comments on papers.

We strongly recommend that AI labs refrain from treating the release of mathematical results as marketing vehicles to promote their models, ignoring the substantial negative externalities that this practice inflicts on the mathematical community.

3. For each result released, the AI lab should make public the name of the model, the prompts used, a (summarized) chain of thought, the time taken, and the estimated cost of computation. Releasing additional material that sheds light on the scientific process that produced the results, such as the initial LLM outputs before they were cleaned up (as recommended in (1) above), is strongly encouraged.

chineseContent:
负责任地发布人工智能生成的数学

目前，一些前沿人工智能实验室正在专有模型上测试高级数学问题，但更广泛的科学界仍然无法访问这些模型。我们的建议是根据实际情况制定的。然而，理想情况下，他们不会这样做。我们想从一开始就明确声明：我们不认可这种做法，我们要求他们停止在专有模型上测试高级数学问题。

数学界对于结果的传播和同行评审有着长期的规范。这些规范对于数学工作的可靠性、可信度和有效性至关重要。数学最重要的学术规范之一是论文的作者应该理解该论文的数学论证，自己验证其正确性，并对内容承担全部责任。此外，在数学界，显着推进该领域发展的著作的作者定期在其他机构举办研讨会并在会议上发表演讲，解释他们的新进展并回答同事的问题。这一切都致力于发展人类对数学最深刻的理解，这是人类发展数千年的最高荣耀之一。

然而，现在的情况是，人工智能可以在没有人类提示的情况下输出数学论证，使其能够理解论证、验证论证或对论证负责。我们相信人类对数学的理解仍然至关重要。在这个新时代，我们如何努力建立一种新范式，将人类对数学的理解作为负责任的学术成果的一部分？

我们向数学界征求反馈，了解人工智能实验室负责任地发布数学结果1意味着什么，并收到了 600 多个回复。根据这些答复，我们提出了一系列建议，并得到了明显多数受访者的支持，针对任何其模型可能对数学产生重大影响的人工智能实验室。这些建议的总体原则如下。

我们在第 2 节中提出了我们的建议，并在第 3 节中对强大模型的访问做出了一些评论。

2. 负责任地发布人工智能实验室产生的结果

我们建议两种可能的行动方案，具体取决于结果所伴随的人类理解水平。

2.A.人类可以理解的论文

由完全理解内容的数学家负责的论文应遵循数学学术界的传统规范：相关数学家应发表预印本，向期刊提交论文供同行评审，并向其他数学家进行演讲以解释其工作。

2.B.尚未被任何人理解的论文

以下建议适用于那些人工智能数学输出不被推动人工智能系统的人理解的实验室。它们分为两部分。第一部分是一套用于发布人工智能生成数学的拟议技术规范。第二部分建议人工智能实验室为人类所需的额外数学活动提供支持，以便人类能够理解和吸收人工智能生成的数学输出并确定其可能的应用。

1. 在法学硕士的帮助下，很容易对人工智能生成结果的初始书面版本进行实质性改进。以下行动应该由人工智能实验室来执行，而不是事后留给数学家。

(a) 应在文献中搜寻与已发布结果证明中的想法相关的任何想法。即使人工智能实验室的模型独立发现了这些想法，它也应该遵循标准的数学实践并引用首次引入这些想法的论文。

(b) 应该提示模型或其他模型生成每个证明的版本，该版本以遵循传统数学论文惯例的风格编写。它们应该包含友好的介绍和精确的定理陈述和证明。它们不应该充满冗长的推理和不标准的术语，导致它们实际上难以理解。

法学硕士目前的能力可能无法重现我们期望的数学家的归因水平或阐述质量，因此释放后可能需要数学家做更多重要的工作才能达到这一标准。如果是这样，则应按照步骤 II 中的描述予以支持。然而，无法达到高标准并不能免除人工智能实验室在上述两点上尽其所能地利用他们的模型的责任。

2. 成果公布后，应及时存入适当的学术知识库。这些不应由任何人工智能实验室控制，并应保证某些标准，包括提交的内容具有持久的可引用标识符，并且后续修改得到适当记录。对于人工智能生成的结果，如果存储库允许对论文进行评论，这将特别有用。

我们强烈建议人工智能实验室不要将数学结果的发布视为推广其模型的营销工具，而忽视这种做法给数学界带来的巨大的负面外部性。

3. 对于每个发布的结果，人工智能实验室应公开模型的名称、使用的提示、（总结的）思路、所花费的时间以及估计的计算成本。强烈鼓励发布更多材料，以阐明产生结果的科学过程，例如清理之前的初始 LLM 输出（如上面 (1) 中的建议）。

4. AI实验室发布的证明应尽可能形式化
